title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Opinions on Protecting the Right to Sue of Parties in Administrative Litigation According to Law
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Protecting Litigants' Right to Sue in Administrative Proceedings in Accordance with the Law

Fa Fa [2009] No. 54

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Opinions on Protecting Litigants' Right to Sue in Administrative Proceedings in Accordance with the Law are hereby issued to you. Please implement them earnestly in light of the actual work.

November 9, 2009

Opinions on Protecting Litigants' Right to Sue in Administrative Proceedings in Accordance with the Law

Since the implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law, the People's Courts have accepted and tried a large number of administrative cases in accordance with the law, effectively resolving administrative disputes, safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of the people, and promoting the law-based administration of administrative organs. The special function of administrative adjudication is becoming increasingly prominent. However, the phenomenon of "difficulty in filing administrative lawsuits" still exists and has become one of the prominent issues strongly reflected by the people. To continuously meet the growing judicial needs of the people and effectively solve the problem of administrative cases not being accepted or addressed, the following opinions are hereby put forward to further emphasize and strengthen the acceptance of administrative cases, protect litigants' procedural rights in accordance with the law, and effectively solve the problem of "difficulty in filing administrative lawsuits":

I. Effectively Raise the Awareness of the Importance of Accepting Administrative Cases

The administrative litigation system is one of the most effective and direct legal systems for safeguarding the interests of the broadest masses of the people. It is an effective means of resolving conflicts among the people under the new situation and an important tool for maintaining social harmony and stability. Whether the channel for accepting administrative cases is unobstructed is the prerequisite for the effective function and role of this excellent judicial system. If the protection of the right to sue is inadequate, it will be difficult to provide effective relief for the legitimate rights and interests of citizens, and the growing judicial needs of the people cannot be met. As the pattern of social interests becomes increasingly diversified and complex, especially under the impact of the international financial crisis, administrative disputes are increasing, becoming more complex and diverse, and some are characterized by suddenness, group nature, and extremism. Only by unblocking the channels for administrative litigation can the people be guided to express their interests in a rational and lawful manner, minimize social disharmony, and enhance understanding and trust between the people and the government. If the litigation channels are blocked, it will inevitably lead to an increase in petitions, intensified irrational behavior, and will seriously affect social harmony and stability, weakening the function of the People's Courts' administrative adjudication in "serving the overall situation and administering justice for the people." People's Courts at all levels must fully understand that judicial power originates from the people, belongs to the people, serves the people, and is subject to the supervision of the people. From the height of implementing the spirit of the Fourth Plenary Session of the Seventeenth Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and realizing the people-oriented nature of justice, they must fully recognize the importance of accepting administrative cases, earnestly handle the acceptance of administrative cases, and effectively solve the problem of "difficulty in filing administrative lawsuits."

II. Do Not Arbitrarily Narrow the Scope of Acceptable Cases or Illegally Add Acceptance Conditions

The Administrative Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, based on China's national conditions and the current level of rule of law development, have designed a practical scope of acceptable administrative cases, which is the legal basis for the People's Courts to accept administrative litigation cases. People's Courts at all levels must fully and accurately understand and apply these provisions and must not arbitrarily limit the scope of acceptable cases under any pretext. Any justiciable matters explicitly stipulated in the Administrative Procedure Law must not be arbitrarily excluded; matters not explicitly stipulated in the Administrative Procedure Law but authorized by individual laws or regulations must also be strictly followed; specific administrative acts that are not explicitly excluded by laws or judicial interpretations should fall within the scope of acceptable cases for the People's Courts' administrative litigation. Not only must the personal and property rights of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations be protected, but also, in response to the need for rights protection, other economic and social rights closely related to personal and property rights that are stipulated by laws and regulations as being actionable must be protected in accordance with the law. All types of "local policies" that restrict the acceptance of administrative litigation must be resolutely eliminated, and it is strictly prohibited to refuse to accept certain types of administrative cases that should be accepted by law under the pretext of serving the central local work or responding to the financial crisis. The provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations regarding the conditions for filing a lawsuit, the qualification of the subject of the lawsuit, and the period for filing a lawsuit must be accurately understood and strictly implemented. No other conditions restricting the parties' right to sue may be stipulated outside the law. The relationship between the right to sue and the right to win the case must be correctly handled, and the parties' procedural rights must not be restricted or deprived merely because their claims are obviously unfounded. The relationship between pre-lawsuit coordination and case filing and trial must be correctly handled. While giving full play to the role of pre-lawsuit coordination, it must not become an additional condition that hinders the parties from exercising their right to sue. The period for filing a lawsuit must be comprehensively and correctly reviewed. For cases where the delay in filing is not attributable to the plaintiff's own reasons, effective relief must be provided in accordance with the law based on the specific circumstances of the case.

III. Actively Accept New Types of Administrative Cases in Accordance with the Law

With the development of the situation and the progress of the rule of law, the forms of administrative acts are constantly enriched, the fields of administrative management are continuously expanding, the judicial needs of the people are growing, and the characteristics of administrative disputes are constantly changing. People's Courts at all levels must deeply understand the living conditions and ideological trends of people from all walks of life, understand the expectations of the people regarding administrative adjudication work, accept various new types of cases arising from this in accordance with the law, and actively respond to the actual judicial needs of the people. They must actively accept, in accordance with the law, new types of cases such as administrative payment, administrative supervision, administrative promises, and administrative omissions; actively accept, in accordance with the law, cases concerning people's livelihood such as education, labor, medical care, and social security; actively accept, in accordance with the law, cases involving citizens' other social rights such as government information disclosure; and actively explore and study the acceptance conditions and judgment methods for public interest litigation cases. For new types of cases where there is uncertainty, the case should be filed first within the statutory period, and if necessary, the superior People's Court should be consulted. Decisions of non-acceptance must not be made arbitrarily.

IV. Improve Working Mechanisms and Work Style

The filing of administrative cases is highly professional. The Case Filing Divisions and Administrative Divisions of the People's Courts at all levels must strengthen coordination, communication, and cooperation in the acceptance of administrative cases. The procedural rules for accepting cases stipulated in the Administrative Procedure Law and judicial interpretations must be strictly followed. For a party's lawsuit, a case must be filed or a ruling made within the statutory period; if it cannot be determined whether to accept the case, it should be accepted first, and if after review it is confirmed that it does not meet the statutory conditions for filing, the lawsuit should be dismissed by ruling. The "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Jurisdiction of Administrative Cases" must be strictly implemented. If a plaintiff files a lawsuit with the People's Court at the next higher level, the higher People's Court should promptly handle it in accordance with the law; if the acceptance conditions are met, it should urge the competent People's Court to file and accept the case, or it may directly file the case and try it itself or designate another People's Court within its jurisdiction to try it. Work style must be improved, convenience measures strengthened, the filing process streamlined, filing methods enriched, and litigation made easier for the people. For urgent cases involving the vital interests of the people or the public interest that meet the filing conditions, the case must be filed promptly and tried as soon as possible. Measures such as litigation guidance, information on rights, and risk warnings should be vigorously promoted. If the lawsuit petition is incomplete or the wrong defendant is listed due to the plaintiff's lack of legal knowledge, necessary guidance and explanation must be provided. Without such guidance and explanation, the lawsuit must not be dismissed on the grounds of non-compliance with the conditions for filing. Judicial openness and transparency must be enhanced. For cases where acceptance is denied or the lawsuit is dismissed in accordance with the law, legal instruments must be issued in accordance with the law, and the legal instruments must provide convincing reasons.

V. Strengthen Supervision Over the Acceptance of Administrative Cases

Higher People's Courts must, through various measures such as hearing appeals and retrial petitions, accepting reports, case evaluations, special inspections, and ranking notifications, further strengthen guidance and supervision over the filing and acceptance of administrative cases by lower People's Courts, effectively preventing incidents where parties resort to petitions everywhere or social conflicts intensify due to their inability to file lawsuits. The performance evaluation method for administrative adjudication must be improved, and the weight of evaluation related to petitions and complaints arising from illegal refusal to accept cases must be increased. The "Measures for Investigating the Responsibility of Judicial Personnel for Illegal Adjudication (for Trial Implementation)" must be strictly implemented. For personnel who, in violation of legal provisions, arbitrarily refuse to accept cases that should be accepted, or who cause serious consequences due to illegal dereliction of duty, they must be dealt with seriously in accordance with laws and discipline. All types of illegal interference with the acceptance of administrative cases must be resolutely resisted, and all kinds of "local policies" that illegally restrict the acceptance of administrative cases must be completely abolished. For acts of interference or obstruction that cause adverse effects on the acceptance of administrative cases by the People's Courts, the situation must be promptly reported to the local Party committee, disciplinary inspection and supervision organs, and the higher People's Court. The higher People's Court should assist the Party committee and disciplinary inspection and supervision organs in handling the matter seriously.

VI. Strive to Create a Favorable External Environment for Filing and Accepting Administrative Cases

Through various means such as typical cases, legal publicity, and litigation guidance, the publicity of the Administrative Procedure Law must be strengthened, the ability and level of parties to participate in administrative litigation must be improved, and the people must be guided to assert their rights in a rational and lawful manner; the quality of handling administrative cases must be effectively improved, efforts must be made to reduce litigation costs, shorten litigation cycles, strengthen enforcement, and enhance the credibility of administrative adjudication; work style must be further improved, service awareness enhanced, service levels raised, and more convenient remedies provided to the people; strong legal protection measures must be taken to severely punish acts of retaliation against parties, enabling the people to dare to use legal means to safeguard their legitimate rights and interests. The government and relevant departments should be advised to correctly understand and evaluate the phenomenon of losing administrative lawsuits, modify and improve relevant evaluation systems, and prevent and eliminate the negative impacts arising therefrom. The leadership of the Party committee and the supervision of the People's Congress must be more proactively and consciously sought, and the support of government organs and all sectors of society must be obtained. Through unremitting efforts, the problems of difficulty in filing, trying, and enforcing administrative cases should be fundamentally resolved, enabling the administrative litigation system to play a more active role in protecting legitimate rights and interests, promoting law-based administration, resolving administrative disputes, and maintaining harmony and stability.
